stories.headline: Iran hits US bases in five countries after American strike on Iranian wedding kills 18

key_facts.fact: Iran's health minister said 18 people were killed and 108 injured in the latest wave of US strikes on Iran on September 2, including four killed at a wedding party in the coastal town of Kuhestak.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran accused Washington of hitting a wedding party, killing four people and wounding dozens. Its health minister later said 18 people in total had been killed and 108 injured in the latest wave of U.S. strikes.

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC said it fired missiles and drones at US facilities in Jordan (Prince Hassan airbase), Bahrain (Sheikh Isa airbase), Kuwait (Ali Al Salem) and Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan region; Jordan said it intercepted 10 of 13 ballistic missiles.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's military said it launched attacks on US bases and assets in Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Iraq's Erbil... Jordanian armed forces said air defence systems intercepted and destroyed 10 of 13 Iranian ballistic missiles.

key_facts.fact: Two weapons experts told the AP that fragments shown by Iranian media from the Kuhestak strike came from a US-made SLAM-ER cruise missile; the dead included two women and two children aged 4 and 16, with at least 68 wounded.
key_facts.excerpt: Four people were killed - two women and two children, aged 4 and 16 - and at least 68 were wounded... Two weapons experts told The Associated Press that images of fragments of a missile... were from a U.S.-made SLAM-ER cruise missile.

key_facts.fact: Iran's currency hit a record low on September 2, with traders in Tehran exchanging 2.20 million rials per US dollar, 10% weaker than the previous week's record.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's currency hit another record low on Wednesday, with traders in Tehran exchanging 2.20 million rials for one U.S. dollar, a 10% hike from last week's record.

key_facts.fact: The US Navy escorted 40 commercial vessels carrying 18 million barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, a wartime high, while fending off drone attacks, two US officials told CNN.
key_facts.excerpt: The US military escorted 40 commercial vessels carrying 18 million barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz, marking a wartime high.

key_facts.fact: Iran struck US bases in Kuwait again on Thursday September 3; Trump said the US could attack Iran 'any time we want' and floated renaming the Strait of Hormuz the 'Trump Strait'.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran attacked US military bases in Kuwait on Thursday... 'Now that we have it under U.S.A. control, should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT???' the US president wrote on Truth Social.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude settled up 98 cents, or 1%, at $95.63 a barrel on September 2 and WTI at $91.01, with intraday highs the strongest since July 24.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures settled up 98 cents, or 1%, at $95.63 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 79 cents, or 0.9%, to settle at $91.01.

stories.headline: US private hiring slows to 38,000 as 10-year yield tops 4.8% and Fed hike odds jump to 64%

key_facts.fact: ADP said US private employers added 38,000 jobs in August, below the 47,000 expected and down from July's revised 46,000 - the slowest pace since January.
key_facts.excerpt: The US private sector added 38,000 jobs in August, according to data provider ADP, marking the slowest pace of job creation since January... The ADP figures for August fell from July's revised 46,000 jobs added, and underperformed economists' expectations of 47,000 jobs.

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield briefly rose above 4.82% on September 2, its highest intraday level since November 2023, while the 30-year held at 5.27%.
key_facts.excerpt: the yield on the 10-year Treasury note... briefly rose to above 4.82% Wednesday, its highest intraday level since November 2023.

key_facts.fact: Traders raised the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike at its September meeting to 64%, up from 37% a week earlier, per CME FedWatch.
key_facts.excerpt: Traders now see a 64% likelihood that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its meeting later this month, up from 37% a week ago, per the CME Group's FedWatch tool.

key_facts.fact: New York Fed President John Williams told CNBC there were 'no clear signs right now' that a September hike would be needed, easing the bond selloff and lifting stocks.
key_facts.excerpt: Market sentiment also improved after New York Fed President John Williams told CNBC that there were 'no clear signs right now' that a September rate hike would be needed to bring down inflation.

key_facts.fact: The Dow rose 0.6% and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each gained about 0.5% on September 2, snapping three-session losing streaks despite elevated oil and yields.
key_facts.excerpt: The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.6%, while the benchmark S&P 500 and tech-focused Nasdaq Composite each gained 0.5%.

key_facts.fact: Economists expect Friday's Bureau of Labor Statistics report to show 53,000 jobs added in August after a loss of 23,000 in July, with unemployment steady at 4.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: A report Friday from the Bureau of Labor Statistics is expected to show U.S. employers added 53,000 jobs last month, after shedding 23,000 jobs in July... The unemployment rate is expected to stay at 4.1%.

stories.headline: Bank of Canada holds at 2.25% for a seventh time, flagging oil and US tariffs as inflation risks

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Canada held its overnight rate target at 2.25% on September 2, with the Bank Rate at 2.5% and the deposit rate at 2.20% - its seventh consecutive hold.
key_facts.excerpt: The Bank of Canada today held its target for the overnight rate at 2.25 per cent, with the Bank Rate at 2.5 per cent and the deposit rate at 2.20 per cent.

key_facts.fact: Canadian GDP grew 3.3% in the second quarter after a very weak first quarter, with unemployment edging down to 6.4% in July.
key_facts.excerpt: Canadian economic activity strengthened in the second quarter, with GDP up by 3.3 per cent, following very weak growth in the first quarter... the unemployment rate edging down to 6.4 per cent in July.

key_facts.fact: CPI inflation has hovered around 3% on high gasoline prices; excluding gasoline it was 2.2% in July, and the bank said upside risks have increased because of the Middle East conflict and 'little progress reopening the Strait of Hormuz'.
key_facts.excerpt: excluding gasoline, inflation was 2.2 per cent... with the Middle East conflict still ongoing and little progress reopening the Strait of Hormuz, upside risks to the Bank's inflation forecast have increased.

key_facts.fact: Governor Tiff Macklem said the goods hit by new US tariffs represent about 5% of Canadian exports to the United States, and that the bigger risk is businesses delaying investment and hiring.
key_facts.excerpt: Affected products represent about 5% of exports to the United States. And the federal government's support programs will likely mitigate some of the harm.

key_facts.fact: Canada's counter-tariffs on nearly $28 billion of US products, ranging from 15% to 50% and covering dairy, steel, copper and some beauty products, take effect September 8, in response to the 50% US duty imposed after talks collapsed in August.
key_facts.excerpt: Canada's counter-tariffs on nearly $28 billion worth of US products are scheduled to begin on Sept. 8. The Canadian tariffs will range from 15 to 50 per cent.

key_facts.fact: Ottawa announced a C$7.5 billion package of relief for businesses and workers hit by the latest round of US tariffs.
key_facts.excerpt: The federal government has announced a new package of relief for businesses and workers affected by Trump's latest round of tariffs. In all, $7.5 billion is being put toward modifying and expanding existing programs.

stories.headline: US tariffs of up to 100% on imported drones take effect, aimed at China's DJI

key_facts.fact: The United States began imposing tariffs of up to 100% on imported drones and critical components at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on September 3, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The United States began imposing tariffs of up to 100% on imported drones and critical components at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on September 3, 2026.

key_facts.fact: The 100% ad valorem duty covers unmanned aircraft with a maximum take-off weight above 25 kg, drones that integrate thermal imagers, docking stations and listed critical components; smaller drones face 25%.
key_facts.excerpt: a 100 percent ad valorem duty rate on the import of UAS with a maximum take-off weight of more than 25 kilograms, UAS that integrate thermal imagers, UAS docking stations, and certain UAS components... a 25 percent ad valorem duty rate on imports of UAS with a maximum take-off weight of 25 kilograms or less.

key_facts.fact: Drones from the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland and Liechtenstein are capped at 15% and UK products at 10%, provided importers certify that substantially all critical components and technology come from those countries or the US.
key_facts.excerpt: For products of Japan, the Republic of Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, or a member nation of the European Union, the duty rate shall be no higher than 15 percent... For products of the United Kingdom, the duty rate shall be no higher than 10 percent.

key_facts.fact: Suppliers on the Pentagon's Blue UAS Cleared List or Blue UAS Framework as of September 2, 2026 are exempt until February 9, 2027, the same date a further 25% duty hits an additional list of components.
key_facts.excerpt: Products and components supplied by companies included on the Pentagon's Blue UAS Cleared List or Blue UAS Framework as of September 2, 2026, will not become subject to the duties until February 9, 2027.

key_facts.fact: The measures came out of a Section 232 national-security investigation opened by the commerce secretary on July 1, 2025, which found US drone makers still depend on foreign motors, electronic speed controllers, lithium-ion batteries and docking stations.
key_facts.excerpt: The tariffs follow a Section 232 investigation initiated by the secretary of commerce on July 1, 2025... US companies manufacturing drones domestically remain dependent on foreign suppliers for motors, electronic speed controllers, lithium-ion batteries and docking stations.

key_facts.fact: Shenzhen-based DJI is estimated to make more than 70% of the world's commercial drones, and the affected models are widely used by US law enforcement to track wildfires and find missing people.
key_facts.excerpt: It is estimated that a single Chinese company - Shenzhen-based DJI - manufactures more than 70 per cent of the world's commercial drones.

stories.headline: uniQure files for FDA and UK approval of AMT-130, the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease

key_facts.fact: uniQure submitted a biologics license application to the FDA for AMT-130 on September 2 and also applied for approval in the United Kingdom.
key_facts.excerpt: After months of regulatory spectacle, uniQure has submitted a biologics license application to the FDA for its Huntington's disease gene therapy. The biotech has also applied for approval of AMT-130 in the United Kingdom.

key_facts.fact: If approved, AMT-130 would be the first genetic treatment for Huntington's disease, an incurable neurodegenerative disorder.
key_facts.excerpt: If approved, AMT-130 would be the first-ever genetic treatment for Huntington's disease.

key_facts.fact: The company requested priority review, which would mean a six-month review after a 60-day filing period and a possible accelerated-approval decision in late April or early May 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: If granted, this would mean a six-month review cycle for AMT-130, following a 60-day BLA review period... FDA could set an action date for the potential accelerated approval in late April or early May 2027.

key_facts.fact: The filing rests on three-year Phase 1/2 data comparing AMT-130 to a propensity-score-matched external control from the Enroll-HD natural history database, which showed a 75% slowing of disease progression.
key_facts.excerpt: UniQure is backing its application with three-year data from a Phase 1/2 trial that compared AMT-130 to a propensity score-matched external control derived from the Enroll-HD natural history database. The data... showed a 75% slowing.

key_facts.fact: A confirmatory trial of about 200 patients randomized 2:1 between AMT-130 and standard of care is expected to be well under way before the FDA rules.
key_facts.excerpt: the study - which will include around 200 patients with 2:1 randomization between AMT-130 and standard of care - 'will be well underway before the FDA gives their decision on accelerated approval'.

stories.headline: Akeso's PD-1/VEGF bispecific beats pembrolizumab on survival in first-line lung cancer

key_facts.fact: Akeso announced on September 2 that a pre-specified interim analysis of the Phase III HARMONi-2 trial met the key secondary endpoint of overall survival, with ivonescimab showing a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement over pembrolizumab.
key_facts.excerpt: a pre-specified interim analysis of overall survival (OS) in the HARMONi-2 (AK112-303) trial, as assessed by the Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC), met the key secondary endpoint of OS. The results demonstrated that ivonescimab showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement over pembrolizumab.

key_facts.fact: HARMONi-2 is a randomized, double-blind registrational trial testing ivonescimab, a first-in-class PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, against pembrolizumab as first-line treatment for advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer with PD-L1 expression of at least 1%.
key_facts.excerpt: HARMONi-2 is a randomized, double-blind, multicenter, registrational Phase III trial evaluating ivonescimab, Akeso's first-in-class PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, versus pembrolizumab as first-line treatment for patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors express PD-L1 (TPS >=1%).

key_facts.fact: The same trial had already met its primary endpoint at an earlier interim analysis, with median progression-free survival of 11.14 months for ivonescimab versus 5.82 months for pembrolizumab.
key_facts.excerpt: ivonescimab met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) in the HARMONi-2 study, with a median PFS of 11.14 months versus 5.82 months for pembrolizumab.

key_facts.fact: The indication was approved in China in 2025, and Hong Kong-listed Akeso now has eight innovative drugs on the market and more than 50 assets in its pipeline.
key_facts.excerpt: In 2025, this indication received regulatory approval in China... the company maintains a robust pipeline of more than 50 innovative assets... Eight innovative drugs are commercially available.

stories.headline: Ukraine's SBU and military intelligence trade fire in Kyiv; Zelensky fires an SBU chief

key_facts.fact: A shootout between Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) and military intelligence (HUR) broke out in Kyiv on the morning of September 2, injuring three HUR officers.
key_facts.excerpt: A shootout between Ukraine's military intelligence agency (HUR) and State Security Service (SBU) broke out in Kyiv the morning of Sept. 2, injuring three HUR officers.

key_facts.fact: The SBU said it was investigating an alleged Russian FSB plot against Stepan Kaplunov, deputy commander of the Russian Volunteer Corps, and that its officers were attacked during searches, prompting it to deploy the Alfa special unit.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the SSU's version, a 'group of people' attacked its officers during searches and investigative actions on September 2, forcing it to deploy the Alfa special unit, whose members wounded the attackers while defending themselves.

key_facts.fact: The commander of HUR's 'Timur' special unit said the SBU had 'kidnapped in broad daylight' a military intelligence commander, held him without charges and then opened fire without warning on unarmed HUR personnel.
key_facts.excerpt: The commander of HUR's special unit 'Timur'... said... Kaplunov had been 'kidnapped in broad daylight' by members of the SBU and held without charges... He alleged that the SBU opened fire on unarmed HUR officers.

key_facts.fact: President Zelensky called the episode 'an absolutely disgraceful situation' and said that 'here in Ukraine, one can shoot only at the Russian occupiers in defense of Ukraine.'
key_facts.excerpt: Zelensky later called the incident 'an absolutely disgraceful situation' involving SBU and HUR units... 'Here in Ukraine, one can shoot only at the Russian occupiers in defense of Ukraine.'

key_facts.fact: Zelensky signed a decree on September 2 dismissing Oleh Khramov, head of the SBU's Department for the Protection of State Secrets and Licensing since March 2023; the decree gave no reason.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy fired senior Ukrainian Security Service (SBU) official Oleh Khramov following a shootout between SBU and HUR officers in Kyiv, according to a presidential decree signed on September 2... who had led the SBU's Department for the Protection of State Secrets and Licensing since March 2023.

key_facts.fact: Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko and the State Bureau of Investigation took over the case, and presidential office head Kyrylo Budanov called for a 'thorough and impartial' investigation.
key_facts.excerpt: The Prosecutor General's Office and the State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) will examine testimony and statements from all individuals linked to the shootout... Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Presidential Office and former HUR chief, called for a thorough investigation.
